title: Smoke testing: does the application even come up?

videos.script: A new build arrives. Before you test anything in it, ask one question: is it worth testing at all? {{question}} A smoke test answers it. It is a short list of checks, the same every time. {{list}} It touches every major part of the product once, on its main path, and goes no deeper. {{wide}} If every check passes, testing starts. If one fails, testing waits. {{gate}} For boxoffice the list has five checks, and you run them by hand and then as a loop of a few lines. {{loop}} The loop is one command, and it prints a line per check. {{run}} Then you stop the server and run it again, and watch all five fail. {{fail}} Five failures, one cause. You rule out your own lab, apply the plan's suspension criterion, and tell the developer once. {{suspend}}
